text:
A dramatic change in tribal revenue occurred in fiscal year 1975 when Westmoreland Resources paid over $1,991,000 in bonuses, advanced royalties, and royalties for coal extracted from the Absaloka Mine in the Ceded Area. This influx of funds increased tribal revenue almost five-fold above fiscal year 1974. Between 1970 and 1973 tribal income had shown a decline ($620,609 to $435,214) because of diminishing returns from oil and gas leases and bonuses. In 1974 timber sales amounted to $94,225, largely accounting for the increase of $125,000 between 1973 and 1974. In 1975, revenues from oil and gas leases and bonuses also increased above their 1974 levels.
The tribal budget had a carry-over of $256,469 in 1975 from the 1974 budget ("Crow Tribal Funds Status," Crow Agency). The tribe estimates a 1976 fiscal year income of $2,021,379 with an estimated carry-over of $850,000 and an income of $1,290,000 from coal royalties. Oil and gas royalties, bonuses and permits are expected to earn $354,333 in fiscal year 1976. Thus, oil, gas, and coal earnings will comprise 81 percent of tribal revenue in fiscal year 1976 ($1,644,333 of a total anticipated income of $2,021,379) ("Crow Tribal Funds Status," Crow Agency). The third largest single source of income for fiscal year 1976 is expected to be grazing permits ($119,198) which will constitute less than 6 percent of the tribal income.
More than 50 percent of total Crow tribal income was used for the operations of the tribal government in 1975. Community services account for 24 percent and economic development for 21 percent of the budget. Capital investment is last with 5 percent.
